home.aboutHeading: How these prayer times are calculated
home.aboutBody: Prayer times are not looked up from a table — they are computed from the sun's position for the exact latitude and longitude of the place you are viewing, then converted to that place's own timezone. That is why a city 100 km east of another shows a slightly earlier Maghrib, and why the times shift a little every day.
home.aboutMethods: Different authorities set the Fajr and Isha angles differently. Each page defaults to the method normally used in that country — Umm al-Qura in Saudi Arabia, Karachi in Pakistan, ISNA in North America — and you can change both the method and the Asr madhab on any city page.
home.aboutAccuracy: Times are astronomical calculations, not an announcement from a mosque. Local committees sometimes adopt a few minutes' difference, particularly for Fajr and Isha. Where your local mosque differs, follow your local mosque.

cityContent.fajrBody: Fajr begins at true dawn, when the sun reaches {angle} below the horizon, and the window closes at sunrise — <t>{sunrise}</t> in {city} on {date}. That leaves {window} to pray Fajr.
cityContent.sunriseBody: Sunrise marks the end of the Fajr window in {city} on {date}. Prayer is avoided during the moments the sun is actually rising, resuming once it has fully cleared the horizon.
cityContent.dhuhrBody: Dhuhr begins just after the sun passes its highest point over {city} and starts to decline. On {date} that is <t>{time}</t>, and the window runs until Asr at <t>{asr}</t>.
cityContent.asrBody: Asr begins when an object's shadow grows to {shadowFactor} its own length plus its shadow at midday. In {city} on {date} that falls at <t>{time}</t>, and the window lasts until sunset at <t>{maghrib}</t>.
cityContent.maghribBody: Maghrib begins the moment the sun sets in {city} — <t>{time}</t> on {date}. It is also when the fast is broken during Ramadan. The window stays open until Isha at <t>{isha}</t>, {gap} later.
cityContent.ishaBody: Isha begins once the evening twilight has faded, with the sun {angle} below the horizon. In {city} on {date} that is <t>{time}</t>, and the window extends until the following Fajr.
cityContent.ishaBodyInterval: Isha is set a fixed {interval} after Maghrib under this method rather than by a sun angle. In {city} on {date} that is <t>{time}</t>, and the window extends until the following Fajr.

cityContent.methodAngles: It places Fajr at a solar depression of {fajrAngle} below the horizon and Isha at {ishaAngle}.
cityContent.methodIshaInterval: It places Fajr at a solar depression of {fajrAngle} below the horizon and sets Isha a fixed {interval} after Maghrib rather than by a sun angle.
cityContent.methodMaghribAngle: Maghrib is adjusted to a solar depression of {maghribAngle} rather than plain sunset.
cityContent.methodMadhabShafi: Asr follows the Shafi position: it begins when an object's shadow equals its own length plus its midday shadow.
cityContent.methodMadhabHanafi: Asr follows the Hanafi position: it begins when an object's shadow reaches twice its own length plus its midday shadow, which makes Asr noticeably later than under the Shafi view.
cityContent.methodChange: You can switch method or madhab using the selector above the table, and your choice is remembered on this device.
cityContent.monthFajr: Fajr in {city} moves from <t>{startTime}</t> on {startDate} to <t>{midTime}</t> by {midDate}, and <t>{endTime}</t> on {endDate}.
cityContent.monthMaghrib: Maghrib moves from <t>{startTime}</t> to <t>{midTime}</t> and then <t>{endTime}</t> across the same days.
cityContent.monthNote: The shift comes from the earth's tilt changing the length of the solar day — which is why a fixed timetable goes stale and these times are recalculated daily.

homeFaq.coverageAnswer: {cities} cities across {countries} countries — every populated place with more than 15,000 residents, from the GeoNames database. Each has its own page with today's five prayer times, sunrise, the Qibla direction and a full month's timetable.
homeFaq.accuracyAnswer: They are computed with the standard astronomical formulas used by the widely-trusted adhan library, from each city's real coordinates and timezone — the same approach mainstream prayer apps use. Fajr and Isha depend on a chosen sun angle, so those two can differ by a few minutes between authorities.
homeFaq.methodQuestion: Can I change the calculation method?
homeFaq.methodAnswer: Yes. Every city page has a method and madhab selector above the times table. Your choice is remembered on that device and applies to every city you visit afterwards.
homeFaq.qiblaQuestion: Does the site show the Qibla direction?
homeFaq.qiblaAnswer: Every city page gives the Qibla as a bearing in degrees from true north, plus the great-circle distance to the Kaaba in Makkah. If you use a magnetic compass, remember to allow for local magnetic declination.

pages.aboutIntro: This site publishes prayer times for every city, state and country we can cover — currently 34,098 populated places across 252 countries, in 17 languages.
pages.aboutHowBody: Prayer times here are not copied from a timetable or fetched from another site. They are calculated for each place from its own latitude, longitude and IANA timezone, using the standard astronomical method the established calculation conventions define. That is why a small town shows different times from the capital 200 km away, and why the times shift by a minute or two each day as the sun's position changes.
pages.aboutMethodBody: Different regions follow different conventions for the sun-angle that marks Fajr and Isha, and different madhabs mark Asr by a different shadow length. Each country page defaults to the convention normally followed there, and you can change both the method and the madhab from any city page — your choice is remembered on your own device.
pages.aboutDataHeading: Where the place data comes from
pages.aboutDataBody: Coordinates, elevation, timezones, administrative regions and native-script place names all come from GeoNames, an open geographical database published under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. We do not alter the underlying geography; we only calculate against it.
pages.aboutAccuracyBody: Astronomical calculation and local religious practice are not always identical. Many mosques announce times a few minutes either side of a calculated value, and some regions apply local adjustments that no formula captures. Where the two differ, follow your local mosque. This site is a reference, not an authority.
pages.contactIntro: Questions, corrections and reports of wrong times are all welcome — particularly the last one.
pages.contactUnavailable: A contact address has not been configured for this site yet.
pages.contactWhatBody: If you are reporting a time that looks wrong, please include the city page link, the time you expected, and where that expectation comes from (your local mosque, a printed timetable, another site). That makes it possible to tell an actual bug from a difference in calculation convention, which are fixed very differently.
pages.contactResponseBody: This is a small operation, so replies are not instant, but genuine corrections are acted on.
pages.privacyIntro: This page describes exactly what this site does with data. It is written to match the site's actual behaviour rather than to cover every possibility, so it is short.
pages.privacyNoAccountBody: There is no sign-up, no login and no contact form. We do not ask for your name, email address or any other personal detail in order to show you prayer times, and there is no database of visitors.
pages.privacyLocationBody: The site does not request your device's GPS location and does not use the browser geolocation permission at all. Prayer times are calculated from the coordinates of the city page you choose to open, not from where you actually are.
pages.privacyCookiesBody: Two cookies are used, both set by this site, both storing only a preference you chose yourself:
pages.privacyCookieMethod: prayer_method — the calculation method you picked, so pages keep using it.
pages.privacyCookieMadhab: prayer_madhab — the madhab you picked for Asr.
pages.privacyCookiesNote: Neither identifies you, both expire after a year, and clearing your browser's cookies removes them. If you never change the method or madhab, neither is ever set.
pages.privacySearchBody: When you type in the search box, the text is sent to this site's own search endpoint to find matching places. Search text is used to answer that request and is not stored against you or shared.
pages.privacyAdsBodyOff: This site currently shows no advertising and includes no advertising or analytics scripts. If that changes, this page will be updated before any such script is added, and it will say which provider is involved and what it sets.
pages.privacyThirdPartyBody: Pages link out to the Google Play Store and Apple App Store, and credit GeoNames. Following any of those links takes you to a service with its own privacy policy, which governs what happens there. We do not share anything about you with them; a link is just a link.
pages.privacyChangesBody: If this policy changes, the date at the top of the page changes with it.
pages.privacyContactBody: If you have a question about any of the above, the contact page explains how to reach us.
pages.termsIntro: Plain terms for a free reference site.
pages.termsUseBody: You may use this site freely for personal and community purposes, including reading times aloud, printing a page, or sharing a link. No permission or attribution is required for that.
pages.termsAccuracyBody: Times here are produced by astronomical calculation. They are offered in good faith and checked against independent references, but they are not a religious ruling and carry no authority over your local mosque's announced times. For anything that matters — fasting, congregational prayer, Ramadan timetables — treat your local mosque as authoritative.
pages.termsNoWarrantyBody: The site is provided as it is, without guarantee that it will always be available, or that every value on every one of its many thousands of pages is correct. Errors are possible; please report them.
pages.termsLiabilityBody: To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for loss arising from relying on times published here. This does not limit any right you have that cannot lawfully be excluded.
pages.termsContentBody: Underlying place data belongs to GeoNames and is used under its Creative Commons Attribution licence. App names, icons and store badges belong to their respective owners and are shown to identify the apps they link to. The written content of these pages belongs to this site.
pages.termsChangesBody: These terms may be updated; the date at the top of the page shows when they last were.
pages.disclaimerIntro: The single most important thing to know about this site.
pages.disclaimerCalcHeading: These times are calculated, not decreed
pages.disclaimerCalcBody: Every time on this site is computed from the sun's position for a given set of coordinates. No scholar reviews the individual pages, and no mosque or religious authority endorses them. They are a mathematical result, presented as one.
pages.disclaimerDifferBody: Legitimate differences arise from the calculation convention in use (regions disagree on the sun-angle for Fajr and Isha), the madhab followed for Asr, deliberate local safety margins, and moon-sighting practice for the Hijri date. A few minutes' difference is normal and is usually not an error on either side.
pages.disclaimerFollowBody: Where this site and your local mosque disagree, follow your local mosque. Use these pages for planning, for travel, and for places where no local timetable is available.
pages.disclaimerHijriBody: The Hijri date shown is produced by tabular conversion and is labelled approximate throughout. Countries that begin months by physical moon sighting will sometimes be a day ahead or behind it. Do not use it to decide when Ramadan or Eid begins.
pages.disclaimerAppsBody: The mobile apps listed on this site are made by other companies. We do not operate them, receive no payment for listing them, and cannot support them. Their ratings and download counts are recorded by hand from their store listings on the date shown and are not live figures.
